title: Private Observability Minimum Pack — Dashboard Wireframes + Panel Inventory (Draft)
body:
Context
- This doc captures rough wireframes + an inventory of panels for the Private Observability Minimum Pack dashboards.
- Target: VPC + on-prem (incl. air-gapped). Must be “day-1 usable” and consistent with Redwood’s supported signals standard.
- Primary Grafana datasource assumed: Prometheus (or compatible). Logs dashboarding is “nice-to-have” panels that link out to customer log backend (Loki/Elastic/Splunk/etc.) where available.

Assumptions / conventions
- All dashboards use a consistent variable template (see “Templating” section).
- Prometheus scrape interval: default 15s; dashboards should render well at 30s.
- Avoid high-cardinality groupings by default; provide optional drill-down panels that are gated behind toggles/variables.

Dashboard set (wireframe-level)
1) Gateway / Inference API Overview (golden signals)
2) Runtime Performance (prefill vs decode + batching/queue)
3) GPU & Node Saturation (util/mem/throttling)
4) Errors & Reliability (error taxonomy + client disconnects)
5) Routing & Fallback (policy decisions + model/region fallback)
6) Control Plane Health (config/policy/auth dependencies)
7) Private Install Health (installer/upgrade controller)

------------------------------
Global templating (all dashboards)
Variables (Grafana)
- $cluster: required. Source label: cluster (or k8s_cluster). Must exist on all exported metrics.
- $namespace: default to “redwood-private” (or install-time namespace). Label: namespace.
- $env: optional (prod/staging). Label: environment.
- $tenant: optional; should be off by default due to cardinality. Label: tenant_id.
- $route: optional; label: route (API route name, not full path).
- $model: optional; label: model (canonical model id), and optionally model_variant.
- $instance: for node/pod drill-down.
- $job: for scrape job selection when customers use their own naming.

Standard time ranges
- Default: last 1h
- Quick ranges: 15m, 1h, 6h, 24h

Panel formatting
- Latency panels show p50/p95/p99 where meaningful.
- Wherever possible, panels include “SLO marker” annotation lines (e.g., p99 budget line, error budget burn threshold).
- Most panels should render on a 1920x1080 operator screen without scrolling horizontally.

Cardinality guardrails
- Avoid “group by request_id”, “group by user_id”, etc.
- Any “Top N” panel that groups by $tenant or $model must be behind a variable and default to “All (aggregated)” view.

------------------------------
1) Dashboard: Gateway / Inference API Overview
Audience: on-call operator / SRE / customer platform team
Goal: quick health check; detect impact (availability, latency, error) + basic throughput and disconnects.

Wireframe (rough)
Row A: “At a glance”
- Stat: Requests/sec (RPS)
- Stat: Active streams (if streaming enabled)
- Stat: p95 end-to-end latency
- Stat: 5xx rate
- Stat: 4xx rate
- Stat: Saturation hint (queue depth or pending requests)

Row B: Latency overview
- Time series: End-to-end latency p50/p95/p99 (all routes)
- Time series: Latency by route (p95) [optional drill-down]
- Heatmap (optional): latency distribution (if we have histogram buckets)

Row C: Errors
- Time series: 5xx rate (overall)
- Bar/pie: 5xx breakdown by error_code (top 10)
- Time series: streaming disconnect rate (client_cancelled / upstream_timeout)

Row D: Traffic / usage
- Time series: requests by route (stacked)
- Time series: tokens out/sec (if emitted at gateway) OR infer from runtime
- Table: top routes by p95 latency (limited rows)

Required metrics (gateway)
- redwood_gateway_requests_total{cluster,namespace,route,method,status_code,tenant_id?}
- redwood_gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster,namespace,route,status_code}
  - Need histogram buckets, not only summaries.
- redwood_gateway_inflight_requests{cluster,namespace}
- redwood_gateway_stream_disconnects_total{cluster,namespace,route,reason}
- redwood_gateway_upstream_timeouts_total{cluster,namespace,route}

Notes / instrumentation gaps
- Ensure route is a stable identifier (e.g., “/v1/chat/completions” => “chat_completions”) to avoid cardinality explosions.
- status_code label should be coarse enough; keep exact code (e.g., 429, 500) but avoid embedding internal error names there.

------------------------------
2) Dashboard: Runtime Performance (prefill vs decode)
Audience: runtime/on-call; performance debugging
Goal: determine whether latency is driven by prefill, decode, queueing, or batching; observe KV cache effectiveness.

Wireframe
Row A: Throughput and queueing
- Time series: tokens generated/sec (decode) aggregated
- Time series: queue depth (pending requests)
- Time series: batch size (avg/p95)
- Time series: scheduler wait time p95

Row B: Latency split
- Time series: prefill latency p50/p95/p99
- Time series: decode latency per token p50/p95/p99 (or decode time)
- Time series: end-to-end service time vs queue time (stacked area if possible)

Row C: Cache / efficiency
- Stat: KV cache hit rate
- Time series: KV cache hit rate
- Time series: prefix cache hit rate (if present)
- Time series: GPU kernel time vs non-kernel time (if emitted)

Row D: “Who’s slow?” (drill-down)
- Table: p95 latency by model (top N)
- Table: p95 latency by node/pod (top N)

Required metrics (runtime/scheduler)
- redwood_runtime_request_latency_seconds_bucket{cluster,namespace,model,phase="prefill|decode|queue"}
  - Ideal: separate histograms for phases; minimum: distinct counters/summary for queue vs service time.
- redwood_runtime_tokens_generated_total{cluster,namespace,model}
- redwood_runtime_tokens_prefilled_total{cluster,namespace,model}
- redwood_scheduler_queue_depth{cluster,namespace,queue}
- redwood_scheduler_wait_seconds_bucket{cluster,namespace,queue}
- redwood_runtime_batch_size{cluster,namespace,model} (gauge or histogram)
- redwood_runtime_kv_cache_hits_total / redwood_runtime_kv_cache_requests_total
- redwood_runtime_prefix_cache_hits_total / redwood_runtime_prefix_cache_requests_total (optional)

Notes / instrumentation gaps
- Need a consistent definition of “prefill” and “decode” that maps to user-perceived latency.
- Ensure model label is canonical (no full path, no sha fragments unless explicitly “model_version”).

------------------------------
3) Dashboard: GPU & Node Saturation
Audience: infra operator; capacity planning; incident response
Goal: show when GPUs/nodes are saturated and correlate with inference latency/errors.

Wireframe
Row A: GPU overview
- Time series: GPU utilization (avg/max)
- Time series: GPU memory used %
- Time series: GPU power/thermal throttling indicator (if available)
- Stat: number of unhealthy GPUs/nodes

Row B: Correlate saturation to user impact
- Time series (overlay): GPU utilization vs p95 latency
- Time series (overlay): GPU memory pressure vs 5xx rate

Row C: Node resources
- Time series: CPU usage % (nodes running gateway/runtime)
- Time series: Memory usage %
- Time series: Disk pressure (if on-prem; local PVs)
- Time series: Network RX/TX (optional)

Row D: “Top offenders”
- Table: GPUs by utilization (top N)
- Table: pods by restart count (top N)

Required metrics
- NVIDIA DCGM exporter style (preferred):
  - DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL{cluster,namespace,instance,gpu}
  - DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED / DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_TOTAL
  - DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_USAGE / DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_LIMIT
  - DCGM_FI_DEV_THERMAL_VIOLATION (if present)
- Kube/state/node exporter (minimum):
  - node_cpu_seconds_total, node_memory_* (with cluster label)
  - kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total
  - kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready"}

Notes
- For on-prem minimal mode, we should be explicit what we support: DCGM exporter is strongly recommended. Without it, GPU dashboards degrade (show “missing metrics” panel).

------------------------------
4) Dashboard: Errors & Reliability
Audience: on-call, Support/TAM during go-live
Goal: isolate whether errors are client-side (4xx), gateway, runtime, model, upstream dependencies; show top error codes + rate changes.

Wireframe
Row A: SLO error rate
- Time series: error rate (5xx / total)
- Time series: availability (1 - 5xx)
- Stat: current burn rate (if computed)

Row B: Error taxonomy
- Bar: 5xx by error_code (top 10)
- Bar: 4xx by reason (auth, quota, validation, rate limit)
- Time series: 429 rate

Row C: Streaming / cancellations
- Time series: client disconnects by reason
- Time series: upstream reset/timeout

Row D: Drill-down tables
- Table: errors by route
- Table: errors by model

Required metrics
- redwood_gateway_requests_total (needs status_code)
- redwood_gateway_errors_total{error_code,route}
- redwood_runtime_errors_total{error_code,model}
- redwood_auth_failures_total (optional, if auth integration emits)

Notes
- We need a controlled error_code vocabulary. Avoid raw exception strings as labels.

------------------------------
5) Dashboard: Routing & Fallback
Audience: Private operators + Redwood support during capacity incidents
Goal: understand policy-based routing, fallbacks, and whether customer requests are being served by intended model/variant/region.

Wireframe
Row A: Routing decisions
- Time series: requests by chosen model (stacked)
- Time series: requests by capacity tier (host pool vs dedicated pool in Private context; if applicable)

Row B: Fallback behavior
- Time series: fallback events total
- Bar: fallback reason (capacity, model unavailable, policy)
- Table: fallback “from -> to” (top N)

Row C: Policy propagation health
- Stat: last policy update timestamp (control plane)
- Time series: policy sync errors

Required metrics
- redwood_router_requests_total{requested_model,chosen_model,route}
- redwood_router_fallback_total{reason,from_model,to_model}
- redwood_policy_sync_success_timestamp_seconds (gauge)
- redwood_policy_sync_errors_total{reason}

Notes
- Make sure requested_model/chosen_model labels are normalized to prevent cardinality blow-ups.

------------------------------
6) Dashboard: Control Plane Health
Audience: Private operator
Goal: make it clear when issues are caused by control plane services (config store, auth integrations, certificate expiry, etc.).

Wireframe
Row A: Service health
- Stat: control plane API availability
- Stat: p95 control plane latency
- Time series: 5xx rate control plane

Row B: Dependencies
- Time series: config/policy store (latency/errors)
- Time series: identity provider integration errors (OIDC/SAML via customer)
- Time series: KMS/HSM integration errors (if enabled)

Row C: Certificates and auth
- Stat: cert days to expiry (if exported)
- Time series: auth token verification failures (rate)

Required metrics
- redwood_controlplane_http_requests_total{service,route,status_code}
- redwood_controlplane_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service,route}
- redwood_dependency_errors_total{dependency,reason}
- redwood_cert_expiry_days{component} (optional but highly desirable)

Notes
- For Private, dependency labels should be a small known set (e.g., “postgres”, “policy_store”, “oidc_provider”, “kms”).

------------------------------
7) Dashboard: Private Install Health (Installer/Upgrade)
Audience: Private operator + Redwood Solutions during upgrades
Goal: detect install/upgrade controller issues, component readiness, and mismatch between pack version and installer version.

Wireframe
Row A: Version and status
- Stat: private installer version
- Stat: observability pack version
- Stat: last successful reconcile time

Row B: Component readiness
- Table: components (gateway/runtime/control plane/prometheus/grafana/log collector) with Ready / NotReady
- Time series: reconcile errors (rate)

Row C: Rule/dashboard provisioning
- Stat: grafana provisioning last success
- Stat: prometheus rule load status
- Time series: rule evaluation errors (if exposed)

Required metrics
- redwood_installer_reconcile_success_timestamp_seconds
- redwood_installer_reconcile_errors_total{component,reason}
- redwood_installer_component_ready{component} (0/1)
- redwood_observability_pack_info{version}
- prometheus_rule_evaluation_failures_total (if available via Prometheus)

Notes
- This dashboard should not assume internet access; avoid panels that require calling external services.

------------------------------
Cross-dashboard “Missing signals” panels (recommended)
We should include a small, repeated row (collapsed by default) that makes it obvious when core metrics are absent.
- Stat: “Gateway metrics present?” (based on absent() checks)
- Stat: “Runtime metrics present?”
- Stat: “GPU metrics present?”
- Stat: “Control plane metrics present?”
- Stat: “Installer health metrics present?”

PromQL sketch (as text; final queries live in repo)
- Example: gateway present
  - absent(sum(rate(redwood_gateway_requests_total[5m])) by (cluster))

------------------------------
Open questions / TODO
1) Histograms vs summaries
- We should standardize on histograms for latency (gateway + runtime phases). If some components still emit summaries, dashboards will be inconsistent.

2) Label schema decisions
- Confirm minimum label set for: tenant_id, route, model, model_version/model_variant.
- Need final decision on whether tenant_id is allowed on core gateway metrics or only on a sampled subset.

3) Token accounting source
- For “tokens/sec” panels: do we emit at gateway, runtime, or both? Prefer runtime as source of truth.

4) On-prem minimal footprint
- Confirm which exporters we ship as part of “minimum pack” vs “recommended” (DCGM exporter, node exporter, kube-state-metrics).

5) Drill-down without cardinality accidents
- Approach: keep default dashboards aggregated; provide a “Drill-down mode” variable that gates panels with groupings by tenant/model/route.

6) Links to logs
- Decide standard log field keys to use for linking from panels (request_id, tenant_id, model, error_code). Needs alignment with structured logging work.

Notes from initial reviews (captured inline during syncs)
- Sean (SRE): prefer an operator-facing dashboard that clearly answers “Is this paging?” in <60 seconds; keep top row very small.
- Nadia (metrics): do not add model_version to every metric by default; use a separate info metric or controlled rollout.
- Allison (standards): all dashboards should explicitly document required metrics + cardinality guidance; include a “supported signals” callout.
- Bruno (installer): pack version must be visible in dashboards and in post-install validation output.

Appendix: Proposed dashboard folder naming
- /Redwood Private/Overview
- /Redwood Private/Runtime
- /Redwood Private/Infrastructure
- /Redwood Private/Control Plane
- /Redwood Private/Installer & Upgrades

Appendix: Panel naming conventions
- Start with a noun + metric context, e.g., “Latency (p50/p95/p99) — End-to-end”, “Errors — 5xx rate”, “GPU Utilization — avg/max”.
- Avoid internal component codenames; use “Gateway”, “Runtime”, “Control Plane” consistently.
